questions.explanation: Multiply and divide the coefficients: 1.2 × 3.0 = 3.6, and 3.6 ÷ 9.0 = 0.4. Combine the powers: −3 + 8 − (−2) = 7, so the result is 0.4 × 10⁷ = 4.0 × 10⁶. 4.0 × 10⁷ rewrites 0.4 as 4 without lowering the exponent, 4.0 × 10⁸ moves the exponent the wrong way, 4.0 × 10² subtracts 2 instead of adding it for the ÷ 10⁻², and 2.5 × 10⁶ divides the coefficients the wrong way round (9 ÷ 3.6).

f(a + 1) = 3(a² + 2a + 1) − 2a − 2 = 3a² + 4a + 1. Subtract f(a) = 3a² − 2a: 3a² + 4a + 1 − 3a² + 2a = 6a + 1. 6a + 3 forgets the −2 from −2(a + 1), 3a² + 4a + 1 is f(a + 1) alone, 1 expands (a + 1)² as a² + 1, and 6a − 1 slips a sign when subtracting f(a).

questions.stem: The data set 14, 9, 22, 17, 9, 31, 12, x has a median of 15. What is x?
questions.explanation: Sorted without x: 9, 9, 12, 14, 17, 22, 31. With 8 values the median is the mean of the 4th and 5th. For a median of 15, x must sit between 14 and 17, so (14 + x)/2 = 15 and x = 16. 15 sets x equal to the median, which gives (14 + 15)/2 = 14.5, 6 makes the mean 15 instead of the median, and 17 or 18 leave 14 and 17 in the middle, a median of 15.5.

questions.stem: What is the domain of f(x) = ln(x + 1)/√(6 − x − x²)?
questions.explanation: The log needs x + 1 > 0, so x > −1. The square root sits in the denominator, so it must be strictly positive: 6 − x − x² > 0, x² + x − 6 < 0, (x + 3)(x − 2) < 0 and −3 < x < 2. Both together: −1 < x < 2. −3 < x < 2 ignores the log, −1 < x ≤ 2 lets the denominator be zero, −3 ≤ x ≤ 2 ignores the log and the zero denominator, and x > −1 ignores the root.

questions.stem: A 20 ft ladder leans against a vertical wall and makes an angle of 68° with the level ground. To the nearest tenth of a foot, how high up the wall does the top of the ladder reach?
questions.explanation: The ladder is the hypotenuse and the height is the side opposite the 68° angle, so height = 20 sin 68° = 20 × 0.9272 = 18.5 ft. 7.5 ft uses cosine, which gives the distance from the wall. 21.6 ft divides by sin 68° instead of multiplying, 8.1 ft divides by tan 68°, and 49.5 ft multiplies by tan 68°, treating the ladder as a leg.

questions.stem: A cosine curve has amplitude 4, period 6π, a maximum at x = 0 and a midline of y = −1. Which equation describes it?
questions.explanation: A cosine with a maximum at x = 0 needs no shift. The period 2π/b = 6π gives b = 1/3, so y = 4 cos(x/3) − 1. cos(3x) has period 2π/3, y = −cos(x/3) + 4 swaps the amplitude and the midline, the sine version starts on the midline instead of at a maximum, and cos(x/6) has period 12π.

questions.stem: Two similar cones have heights of 4 cm and 10 cm. The smaller cone has a volume of 24 cm³. What is the volume of the larger cone?
questions.explanation: The length ratio is 10/4 = 2.5, and volumes scale by its cube: 24 × 2.5³ = 24 × 15.625 = 375 cm³. 60 scales by 2.5 once, 150 scales by 2.5², which is the area ratio, 9.6 divides by 2.5, and 937.5 uses the fourth power.

questions.stem: What are the period and the phase shift of y = 5 cos(πx/2 + π/4) − 3?
questions.explanation: Factor out b = π/2: y = 5 cos((π/2)(x + 1/2)) − 3. Period = 2π ÷ (π/2) = 4, and the shift is 1/2 unit to the left. Shift π/4 reads the constant without dividing by b, period 1/4 divides b by 2π instead, shift right ignores the plus sign, and period π uses 2π ÷ 2, dropping the π inside b.

questions.stem: A car speeds up uniformly from 12 m/s to 30 m/s while covering 150 m. What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: With no time given, use v² = u² + 2ad: a = (30² − 12²) ÷ (2 × 150) = (900 − 144) ÷ 300 = 2.52 m/s². 5.04 drops the 2, 3.48 adds the squares instead of subtracting, 1.08 squares the change in speed (18²) instead of subtracting the squares, and 0.06 forgets to square at all.

questions.stem: A 4.0 kg rifle fires a 10 g bullet at 800 m/s. What is the rifle's recoil speed?
questions.explanation: Total momentum stays zero: 0.010 kg × 800 m/s = 8.0 kg·m/s, so the rifle moves back at 8.0 ÷ 4.0 = 2.0 m/s. 20 m/s writes 10 g as 0.10 kg, 0.20 m/s writes it as 0.001 kg, 2,000 m/s uses 10 kg, and 8.0 m/s is the bullet's momentum, not divided by the rifle's mass.

questions.stem: A rigid steel tank holds gas at 27 °C and 200 kPa (absolute). The tank is heated to 127 °C. What is the new pressure?
questions.explanation: At constant volume, P ∝ absolute temperature. Convert: 27 °C = 300 K and 127 °C = 400 K, so P = 200 × 400 ÷ 300 = 267 kPa. 941 kPa uses Celsius in the ratio (127 ÷ 27), 150 kPa inverts the ratio, 200 kPa forgets that a rigid tank's pressure rises, and 300 kPa adds 100 kPa for 100 degrees.

questions.stem: A 25 kg crate rests on a ramp tilted at 20°. The coefficient of static friction is 0.40. Using sin 20° = 0.342, cos 20° = 0.940 and g = 9.8 m/s², what is the friction force on the crate?
questions.explanation: Check sliding first: the down-slope pull is 245 × 0.342 = 83.8 N, while static friction can supply up to 0.40 × 245 × 0.940 = 92.1 N. The crate stays put, so friction only needs to match the pull: 83.8 N. 92.1 N is the maximum possible, not the actual, friction, 230 N is the normal force, 98.0 N takes μ times the full weight, and 0 N wrongly assumes friction acts only when something slides.

questions.stem: An ion of iron-56 (atomic number 26) has 23 electrons. What are its charge and its number of neutrons?
questions.explanation: Atomic number 26 means 26 protons. Charge = protons − electrons = 26 − 23 = +3, and neutrons = mass number − protons = 56 − 26 = 30. Fe³⁻ gets the sign backwards (losing electrons makes a positive ion), 26 neutrons assumes neutrons equal protons, 33 neutrons subtracts the electrons from 56, and Fe²⁺ assumes iron's other common ion instead of counting.

questions.stem: How many moles of gas are in a 4.10 L container at 2.00 atm and 27 °C? (R = 0.0821 L·atm/(mol·K))
questions.explanation: n = PV ÷ RT = (2.00 × 4.10) ÷ (0.0821 × 300) = 8.20 ÷ 24.6 = 0.333 mol. 3.70 mol uses 27 instead of 300 K, 0.166 mol leaves out the pressure, 3.00 mol computes RT ÷ PV, and 0.366 mol uses 273 K (STP temperature) instead of the actual 300 K.

questions.stem: A helium-4 nucleus has a mass of 4.00150 u (the neutral atom is 4.00260 u). A proton is 1.00728 u and a neutron is 1.00866 u. What is the nuclear binding energy? (1 u = 931.5 MeV)
questions.explanation: Separate nucleons: 2(1.00728) + 2(1.00866) = 4.03188 u. Mass defect = 4.03188 − 4.00150 = 0.03038 u, and 0.03038 × 931.5 = 28.3 MeV. 7.07 MeV is the binding energy per nucleon, 3,727 MeV converts the whole nucleus mass, 0.0304 MeV forgets the 931.5 conversion, and 27.3 MeV uses the neutral atom's mass, which includes two electrons the proton masses leave out.

questions.stem: An airbag inflates by 2NaN₃ → 2Na + 3N₂. What mass of NaN₃ is needed to make 65.0 L of N₂ at 25 °C and 1.10 atm? (Na 23.0, N 14.0, R = 0.0821 L·atm/(mol·K))
questions.explanation: n(N₂) = PV/RT = 1.10 × 65.0 ÷ (0.0821 × 298) = 2.92 mol. NaN₃ = 2.92 × 2/3 = 1.95 mol × 65.0 g/mol = 127 g. 190 g uses a 1 : 1 ratio, 285 g inverts the ratio (3/2), 1,510 g uses 25 instead of 298 K, and 115 g leaves out the 1.10 atm pressure.
